 PRESENT  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY
By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of CrPC with a prayer for quashing the entire criminal proceedings including the order dated 27.01.2023 passed by learned JMFC, Sahibganj by which, learned JMFC, Sahibganj has taken Abhishek Kumar @ Avishek Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92583421/
1 cognizance against the petitioners for having committed the offences punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P.Act, 1961 in connection with Complaint Case no. 492 of 2018.

sentences.text: 3. This case has a chequered history.

Learned CJM, Sahibganj considering the materials in the record, including the statement on Solemn Affirmation of the complainant and the statements of the enquiry witnesses, vide order dated 18.12.2019 passed in Complaint case no. 492 of 2018, found prima facie case against the petitioner no. 1 for having committed the offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC only.
The petitioner no. 1 has no grievance against the said order passed and he never challenged the said order.

The complainant, who is the opp. party no. 2 of this criminal miscellaneous petition, being aggrieved by the said order dated 18.12.2019 passed by learned CJM,
Sahibganj in Complaint case no. 492 of 2018, filed Criminal Revision No. 21 of 2020, contending therein that learned CJM, Sahibganj has committed an error by not taking cognizance against the petitioner no. 2 who is the father of the petitioner no. 1 and for not taking cognizance for the offence punishable under Section 4 of the D.P.Act, 1961 and vide order dated 09.11.2022

, learned Sessions Judge, Sahibganj made a categorical finding that the materials against the petitioner no. 2 of this criminal miscellaneous petition, is also available in the record on the point of demand of dowry of Rs. 20,00,000/- and the learned CJM, could not be able to see the materials available in the enquiry evidence as well as the Statement on Solemn Affirmation of the complainant against the petitioner no. 2 of this case, at the time of the passing the summoning order dated 18.12.2019 and was of the considered view that the order dated 18.12.2019 passed by learned CJM, Sahibganj is not sustainable in eyes of law and set aside the same and directed the court concerned to pass a fresh summoning order on the basis of the materials available in the record.

The petitioners have no grievance against the order dated 09.11.2022 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Sahibganj in Cr.
Revision no. 21 of 2020 and the petitioners never challenged the said order.
Subsequent to the same, on 27.01.2023, the matter was placed before learned JMFC, Sahibganj.

Learned Judicial Magistrate considered the materials available in the record of demand of dowry of Rs.20,00,000/-
and treatment of cruelty meted out to the complainant -victim and harassment caused to her by coercing the complainant -victim and her father to meet the unlawful demand of Rs. 20,00,000/-
and considering the same, learned Magistrate, vide order dated 27.01.2023 passed in Complaint case no. 492 of 2018 has found prima facie case for the offences punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P.Act,1961 against both the petitioners.
4. It submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that no case under Section 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P.Act,1961 is made out against the petitioners.

The petitioners took a plea of defence that since the complainant is a self-made lady and admittedly, she has no physical relationship with her husband and she is residing separately since November 2017 and since then,
she is not having any relationship with her husband and as the allegations against the petitioners are false, the entire criminal proceedings including the order dated 27.01.2023 passed by learned JMFC,
Sahibganj in connection with Complaint Case no. 492 of 2018 be quashed and set aside.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners also took another defence plea by making allegations against the complainant that the complainant rubbed off the sindoor from her forehead and removed her bangles and she has refused to restore her conjugal life with the petitioner no. 1, hence, on this additional ground also, the entire criminal proceedings including the order dated 27.01.2023 passed Abhishek Kumar @ Avishek Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92583421/
2 by learned JMFC, Sahibganj in connection with Complaint Case no. 492 of 2018 be quashed and set aside.
6.

sentences.text: Learned Special PP and learned counsel for the opp. party no. 2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer of the petitioners of quashing the entire criminal proceedings including the order dated 27.01.2023 passed by learned JMFC, Sahibganj in connection with Complaint Case no. 492 of 2018 and submits that the undisputed fact remains that the petitioner no. 1 never challenged the order dated 18.12.2019 passed by learned CJM, Sahibganj by which, learned CJM, Sahibganj found prima facie case for the offences punishable under Sections 498A of IPC and ordered for issuance of summon to him.

It is then submitted that, as on the selfsame materials, when the petitioner no. 1 acquiesced by not challenging the order taking cognizance, now in view of the further observation made by learned Sessions Judge, in Cr. Rev. no. 21 of 2020 dated 09.11.2022 which order is also not challenged and which order has further fortified the cognizance order, it is not open for petitioner no. 1 to challenge this order by which, prima facie case has been found by learned Magistrate for having committed the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC besides the offence punishable under Section 4 of the D.P.Act,1961, in view of the categorical observation made by learned Sessions Judge in Criminal Revision No. 21 of 2020 wherein, learned Sessions Judge, has categorically found the materials in the record to show that the petitioner no. 2 made dowry demand of Rs.
20,00,000/-; as the same was binding upon the learned Magistrate.

It is next submitted that in view of the undisputed fact that there are materials in the record to constitute the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC as well as under Section 4 of the D.P.Act, 1961 hence, no illegality has been committed by learned Magistrate, in finding the prima facie case in passing the order for issuance of summons.

It is next submitted that certainly the veracity of the defence of the petitioners cannot be considered at this stage, by holding a mini trial to quash the entire criminal proceeding, hence, this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

7. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that petitioner no. 1 has no grievance in respect of the order dated 18.12.2019, by which, learned CJM, has found the prima facie case under Section 498A of IPC against him and ordered for issuance of summon.

The petitioners have no grievance about the finding given by learned Sessions Judge, in passing the order dated 09.11.2022,
passed in Cr. Rev. no. 21 of 2020, wherein learned Sessions Judge, Sahibganj has found that the material in the records suggests that the petitioner no. 2 made dowry demand of Rs. 20,00,000/-
and that observation of the learned Sessions Judge that learned lower court failed to take note of the evidence available in the record.

The said finding and observation of the learned Sessions Judge,
Sahebganj is not under challenge, so the undisputed fact remains that there is allegation against the petitioner no. 2 of making dowry demand of Rs. 20,00,000/- and inter alia causing harassment to the complainant, who is undisputedly the wife of the petitioner no. 1 and daughter- in-law of the petitioner no. 2 with a view to coerce the complainant and her father to meet the unlawful demand of Rs. 20,00,000/- by the petitioners.

In view of this undisputed facts, this court do not find any illegality having been committed by the learned JMFC, Sahibganj in finding the prima facie case for the offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P.Act.

So far as the contention of the petitioners regarding their defence is concerned, it is a settled principle of law that High Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of CrPC, should not enter into a mini trial and embark upon enquiry as to whether the evidence is reliable or not as that would be the function of the trial court, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of State of M.P. v. Awadh Kishore Gupta and Others reported in (2004) 1 SCC 691.

entities.text: State of M.P. v. Awadh Kishore Gupta and Others reported in (2004) 1 SCC 691
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also a settled principle of law that the High Court while exercising its inherent power under Section 482 of CrPC, should not stifle a legitimate prosecution as has been observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Monica Kumar (Dr.) and Another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2008) 8 SCC 781.
9.

entities.text: Monica Kumar (Dr.) and Another v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2008) 8 SCC 781
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, as the undisputed fact remains that there is material in the record to constitute the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Section 4 of the D.P.Act,1961 against the petitioners, in the considered opinion of this Court, this is not a fit case where the entire criminal proceedings in connection with Complaint Case no. 492 of 2018 be quashed and set aside on the basis of defence plea of the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous petition.
10. Accordingly, this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit is dismissed.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated, the 10th June, 2024 Smita /AFR Abhishek Kumar @ Avishek Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92583421/
